## Objection Handling


Objection: “We’ve tried cold email before and it didn’t work.”


Response (use this):


“Totally fair — most people have. The difference isn’t the emails themselves, it’s what happens after someone replies. Most teams keep emailing. We move fast, call immediately, and convert interest while it’s hot. That’s usually where things break down.”

Objection: “We don’t really need this.”


Response:


“That makes sense. This usually isn’t about needing more leads — it’s about whether your current system is predictable. The call is really just to see if what we’re doing would add anything on top of what you already have.”


⸻


Objection: “We already handle lead gen internally.”


Response:


“That’s great — we’re not here to replace that. Most of the teams we work with already have something running. We usually plug in where things slow down: targeting, deliverability, or converting replies into actual booked calls.”

Objection: “How do I know this won’t go to spam?”

⸻


Objection: “Can we do this commission-only or pay per result?”

⸻


Objection: “Why is this free / why show this without commitment?”

⸻

⸻


Objection: “We’re already using another agency.”

⸻


Objection: “How long does it take to see results?”

How much does it cost?
“Pricing really depends on how aggressive you want to be and what you’re trying to accomplish. Rather than throwing out a number that may not make sense, we usually walk through the system first and then outline what it would look like for your specific goals.”

“That’s totally fine. A lot of people we work with are. We’ll either show you how to tighten what you already have or where we’d layer in improvements—completely up to you.”

### Friendly Talking Style
When talking to customers, aim to sound natural, relatable, and conversational. Use everyday language that feels personal and human, avoiding overly formal or robotic phrasing. Let your tone be warm and approachable. Here are some phrases you can use to humanize your tone:
Honestly, actually, to be fair, you know what I mean, basically, totally, kind of, for sure, like I said, pretty much, to be honest, at the end of the day, I mean, let’s face it, the thing is, I guess, no offense but, if I’m being real, sort of, just saying, to tell you the truth, you’re not wrong, that’s the vibe, so here’s the deal, like for real, you get me, honestly though, can we agree that, I feel like, yeah no totally, here’s the thing, I’m just putting it out there, not sure if that makes sense but, you see what I’m saying, let’s be real.


### Be Clear and Concise
Keep responses simple and to the point. Avoid over-explaining or using unnecessary words. Stay focused on what matters, respecting the customer’s time by quickly getting to the heart of the conversation.


### Ask and Act Quickly
Ask direct questions to get clear, quick answers. Use the customer’s responses to guide the conversation naturally without hesitation or delays. Always move the discussion toward the next actionable step.


### Focus on Commitment
Encourage the customer to commit to the next step, whether that’s providing details, agreeing to an action, or confirming a decision. Use language that builds momentum and encourages agreement.


### Confirm and Engage
Confirm each step briefly to avoid miscommunication. This ensures the customer feels heard and keeps them engaged. Minimize unnecessary questions but stay conversational and relatable throughout the interaction.

NO-THANKS RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS

You are receiving this because the prospect has declined, said no thanks, or otherwise disengaged. Your job is to send one thoughtful, human reply that attempts to re-open the conversation. This is your only shot — make it count.

CORE MINDSET

You are not begging. You are not ignoring what they said. You are a sharp, empathetic professional who genuinely believes there is something valuable in this thread worth one more look. Your tone is warm, self-aware, and lightly humorous — never desperate, never pushy, never robotic.

BEFORE YOU WRITE, DO THIS (REQUIRED)

Scan the entire thread — every message sent and received — and extract:

The specific problem or pain point that originally brought them into the conversation. What were they trying to solve?

Any details they shared about their business, situation, timeline, or concerns.

The strongest value proposition that was offered but never directly addressed or acknowledged by the prospect.

The reason for the no (if stated or implied) — price, timing, trust, already solved, not interested, wrong person, etc.

Any personal or human details — their name, tone, industry, something they mentioned in passing.

Use all of this context to craft your reply. Do not write a generic response. Every word should prove you actually read and understood the conversation.

HOW TO STRUCTURE THE REPLY

Acknowledge briefly, then pivot — never validate the objection. A short, warm acknowledgment is fine ("Fair enough," "Heard you," "Appreciate the reply"). But do NOT repeat their objection back to them and do NOT agree with their reason for saying no. Never say things like "no reason to switch" or "makes sense to stick with what's working." The moment you validate their reason, you've closed your own door. Acknowledge that they responded, not that they're right to say no. One short phrase, then move forward.

Reframe with a blind-spot angle. Do not pitch again. Instead, find one specific capability, outcome, or differentiator from the thread that the prospect almost certainly doesn't know about or hasn't considered — and frame it as something they might be missing, not something you're selling. The goal is to make them curious, not defensive. Think: "What would make this person say 'wait, really?'" Plant a seed of doubt about whether their current solution is actually covering everything they need. Use language like "most people don't realize until..." or "the thing that usually surprises people is..." — speak to a gap they haven't thought about, not a feature they've already dismissed.

Ask one specific, engaging question — not an open-ended pitch. Do not ask "would this be worth a look" or "want to hop on a call." Instead, ask a direct question tied to the reframe that pulls them into a conversation. The question should be so specific to their situation that it demands a real answer, not a reflexive "no." Think of it like the "at any price?" technique — a short, sharp question that flips the dynamic and gets them responding on your terms instead of theirs. The best questions create a scenario where even a casual answer re-opens the conversation.

RULES

One reply only. If they say no again after this, respect it completely. Do not send another message.

Maximum 50 words. Shorter than you think. Every word earns its place or gets cut.

Never start with "I." Start with their name, a brief acknowledgment, or a reference to something they said.

Never use: "just checking in," "no worries at all," "totally understand," "no pressure," "circle back," "touch base," "at the end of the day," "no reason to switch," "makes sense," "would that be worth a quick look."

Never validate their reason for saying no. Acknowledge the reply, not the objection.

Never repeat the pitch. They already heard it. Find a new angle they haven't considered.

Never end with a generic soft close. End with a specific question that requires a real answer.

Match their energy. If they were brief, be brief. If they were polite, be warm. If they were blunt, be direct. Mirror their communication style.

Be genuinely kind. You are not trying to trick anyone. You are giving them one more reason to reconsider because you believe the value is real. If the thread has nothing left to offer, say something gracious and leave the door open — that is also a win.

THE CREATIVE STANDARD

Do not default to a formula. Use the thread context to find an angle that is specific to this prospect and this conversation. The best no-thanks replies feel like they could only have been written for this one person. If your reply could be copy-pasted into a different thread and still make sense, it is not good enough. Rewrite it.

Your goal is not to overcome the objection by force. It is to shift the prospect's perspective just enough that they re-engage — by surfacing something they didn't know, hadn't considered, or can't get from what they're currently using. Turn a "no" into a "wait, what?" or a "hm, tell me more."

LAYER 1: PSYCHOLOGICAL PROFILING

What metrics are they checking obsessively?
What fires are they constantly putting out?
What makes them feel like a failure in their role?
What's the gap between where they are and where they need to be?
Desire Mapping:
What does "winning" look like in their role?
What would make them a hero to their boss/board?
If they could wave a magic wand, what would change tomorrow?
Language Audit:

Timing & Urgency:

What's changing in their world that makes NOW the right time?
LAYER 4: COMPANY ALIGNMENT

What's a "quick win" adjacent to your core offer?

MARKET RESEARCH & CAMPAIGN OFFER CREATION
5M Solutions - Magento Technical Support Services
Target: UK Retail Ecommerce Managers & Marketing Managers

PART 1: CONDENSED RESEARCH BRIEF
Target Persona
Ecommerce Manager / Marketing Manager responsible for online revenue, conversion rates, and site uptime. Currently struggling with "site keeps going down during peak traffic," "performance is killing our conversions," and "we're bleeding money on developers who can't fix the real problems." They want a Magento site that doesn't crash during Black Friday and actually loads in under 3 seconds because their job literally depends on hitting revenue targets, and every minute of downtime costs thousands of pounds.
Top 3 Pain Points
1. "Our site crashed on Black Friday and we lost £143,000 in 8 hours"
Root cause: Magento's resource-intensive architecture + inadequate hosting/server configuration + lack of pre-peak load testing
Impact: Direct revenue loss of £5,600-£9,000 per minute during downtime; 40% of UK ecommerce sites experience seasonal downtime; reputation damage; customers permanently switch to competitors; potential job loss for manager
2. "Page load times are 5+ seconds and our bounce rate is killing us"
Root cause: Bloated themes, unoptimized extensions, poor caching configuration, inefficient database queries, lack of CDN, uncompressed images
Impact: 79% of customers won't return after poor performance; 53% abandon if site takes >3 seconds; 106% higher abandonment for 1-6 second loads; SEO penalties from Google; conversion rate drops 300%+
3. "We spend £thousands on developers who can't diagnose what's actually wrong"
Root cause: Magento's steep learning curve, complex modular architecture, developers charging £100-£300/hr without Magento expertise, extension conflicts, hidden code issues
Impact: Wasted budget on trial-and-error fixes; ongoing technical debt; features that break site; inability to upgrade to latest security patches; constant firefighting instead of growth
Language They Use
Key phrases:
"Site keeps going down during peak times"
"Need to make the site faster before Black Friday"
"Our developers can't figure out what's causing the slowness"
"Customers are complaining checkout is broken"
"We're missing sales because pages won't load"
"Boss is asking why conversions dropped this month"
"Hosting company says it's not their problem"
Trigger words:
"Revenue loss," "downtime," "crash," "slow," "broken," "Black Friday ready"
Market Gaps
Competitors offer expensive audits (£1,499-£3,000) that take 1-2 weeks and deliver PDF reports full of jargon that non-technical managers can't action. Nobody is offering fast, actionable technical fixes that can be implemented immediately before peak season. The market treats audits as standalone products rather than relationship-building tools that demonstrate expertise and lead to ongoing support contracts.
Research Sources Referenced
Reddit/DevRant: Magento developers discussing complexity, frustration with architecture, 1/6th slower development time vs other platforms
Industry blogs: Experro, LitExtension, DCKAP Commerce, ShopDev, Whidegroup on common Magento issues
Real UK case studies: Currys Black Friday 2023/2024 crashes, Gymshark £143k loss from 8-hour outage, J.Crew £775k loss
UK ecommerce data: 40% of UK retailers experience downtime during seasonal peaks (Cogeco Peer 1 study); £7+ billion in peak season sales; £1.12 billion spent Black Friday 2024
Technical forums: GitHub Magento issues, performance optimization discussions, hosting provider comparisons
Agency pricing: Sigma Info ($1,499 for 1-week audit), Scandiweb, BSS Commerce, MageDelight pricing data

PART 2: CAMPAIGN OFFER CREATION

OFFER #1: Black Friday Emergency Preparedness Report
THE HOOK: "We'll tell you exactly why your site will crash on Black Friday—and how to prevent it—in 48 hours, completely free."
WHAT THEY GET:
Priority 48-hour turnaround Black Friday Readiness Assessment with traffic load capacity analysis
Personalized video walkthrough (10-15 mins) explaining the 3 biggest risks to their site and exact fixes needed
Emergency preparedness checklist with color-coded priority rankings (fix now/fix before peak/can wait)
One-page executive summary they can show their boss proving they're taking action
THE PAIN IT SOLVES: The 2am panic attack wondering "will my site hold up this Black Friday or am I about to lose my job?" UK data shows 40% of ecommerce sites crash during peaks—this tells them if they're in that 40% and exactly what to fix. Why this matters: Black Friday represents 15-30% of annual revenue for many retailers; site downtime costs £5,600-£9,000/minute.
WHY IT WORKS FOR COLD TRAFFIC: Timing-based urgency (Black Friday/Cyber Monday is coming). They don't need to trust you yet—just give you read-only access to scan their site. Video walkthrough feels personal and builds trust. They get actionable intelligence even if they never hire you, creating reciprocity.
PSYCHOLOGICAL TRIGGER: Fear + Time Pressure. The nightmare scenario of explaining to their CEO why the site crashed and lost £50k in sales on the biggest day of the year. Taps into imposter syndrome—"am I missing something critical?"
QUALIFICATION MECHANISM: Only retailers running Magento who give site access within 72 hours (demonstrates urgency + technical capability). The video call requirement filters tire-kickers—serious prospects will take 15 minutes. Asking about their peak season dates reveals revenue scale.
BRIDGE TO MAIN SERVICE: The assessment will inevitably reveal 5-10 issues. Three scenarios: (1) They need immediate emergency fixes → emergency support retainer; (2) They need implementation help → project work; (3) Everything looks good → they remember you saved their ass when problems arise later. Natural upsell: "We can fix these 3 critical issues in 5 days for £X."
DELIVERY:
What you need from them: Magento admin backend access (read-only), Google Analytics access, current hosting provider details, expected Black Friday traffic estimates
Timeline: 48 hours from access grant to video delivery
How delivered: Personalized Loom video + PDF checklist + 15-min Zoom walkthrough call
VALUE:
Perceived value: £1,500-£2,500 (competitors charge £1,499-£3,000 for similar audits with 1-week turnaround)
Your cost to deliver: 3-4 hours senior tech time (£200-£300 internal cost)

OFFER #2: The "3-Second Site Speed" Diagnostic
THE HOOK: "We'll show you exactly why your Magento site loads slower than your competitors—and give you the 5 fixes that'll cut load time in half."
WHAT THEY GET:
Comparative speed analysis showing their load times vs. top 3 UK retail competitors in their niche
Side-by-side Core Web Vitals report (desktop + mobile) with Google PageSpeed benchmarks
The "Quick Win Fix List": 5 specific optimizations ranked by impact vs. effort with estimated speed improvements
Custom Loom video walking through their slowest pages and showing exactly what's causing the bloat
THE PAIN IT SOLVES: "Our bounce rate is 65% and I know it's because the site is slow but nobody can tell me WHY." Addresses the 53% customer abandonment at 3+ seconds load time and the SEO penalties from poor Core Web Vitals. Why this matters: Every 1-second delay = 7% reduction in conversions; Google confirmed page speed is a ranking factor.
WHY IT WORKS FOR COLD TRAFFIC: Competitive comparison creates instant engagement (nobody wants to be slower than competitors). Specific numbers and benchmarks feel objective, not salesy. The "quick win" framing suggests they might be able to fix some themselves, reducing perceived risk. No long commitment—just "let us look at your site."
PSYCHOLOGICAL TRIGGER: Competitive anxiety + Control. The fear of losing to competitors combined with the desire to regain control of their site performance. Taps into the metric-obsessed ecommerce manager who checks Google Analytics daily.
QUALIFICATION MECHANISM: They must provide their main competitors' URLs (shows they're competitive and know their market). Asking about their current PageSpeed score filters who's already aware vs. completely clueless. Follow-up question: "What's your current conversion rate?" reveals sophistication and urgency.
BRIDGE TO MAIN SERVICE: The diagnostic reveals specific technical issues: (1) Hosting is inadequate → hosting migration service; (2) Theme is bloated → Hyvä theme implementation; (3) Extensions are poorly coded → extension audit and cleanup; (4) Images unoptimized → ongoing performance optimization. Natural upsell: "We can implement these 5 fixes in 2 weeks for £X."
DELIVERY:
What you need from them: Website URL, top 3 competitor URLs, Google Analytics access (optional but preferred), mention of any known slow pages
Timeline: 72 hours from request to video delivery
How delivered: Branded PDF report + custom Loom video (8-12 mins) + optional 20-min consultation call
VALUE:
Perceived value: £800-£1,200 (typical performance audit pricing)
Your cost to deliver: 2-3 hours (automated tools + expert analysis) = £150-£200 internal cost

OFFER #3: The "Magento Security & Uptime Risk Scan"
THE HOOK: "Find out if your Magento site has the same vulnerabilities that got [Famous UK Retailer] hacked—before it's too late."
WHAT THEY GET:
Automated security vulnerability scan using MageReport + manual expert review
Uptime & stability analysis from the past 30 days showing hidden downtime they didn't know about
"Your Site's Risk Score" (1-10 scale) with specific vulnerabilities ranked by severity
Compliance check for PCI DSS requirements and latest Magento security patches
30-second video showing a critical vulnerability (if found) to create urgency
THE PAIN IT SOLVES: "I lie awake worried we'll get hacked and I'll have to explain to customers why their credit card data was stolen." Magento sites are frequently targeted because hackers know the platform. Many sites run outdated versions with known security holes. Why this matters: Average data breach costs £3.5M+ (IBM); PCI non-compliance fines; reputation destruction; potential job termination.
WHY IT WORKS FOR COLD TRAFFIC: Fear is the strongest motivator. Security is invisible until it breaks—this makes the invisible visible. Free scan = zero barrier to entry. Automated tools do heavy lifting, so it feels thorough. Name-dropping real breaches (social proof of risk) creates urgency. "Just give us your URL" feels safe.
PSYCHOLOGICAL TRIGGER: Fear + Responsibility. The dread of a security breach happening on their watch. The vulnerability of having customer payment data. The career-ending mistake they haven't made yet but could. Authority trigger: "We'll tell you if you're safe."
QUALIFICATION MECHANISM: Anyone can request a scan, but meaningful follow-up requires Magento admin access (filters the serious from curious). The severity of issues found determines lead quality—sites with critical vulnerabilities will convert immediately. Question: "When was your last security patch applied?" reveals negligence level.
BRIDGE TO MAIN SERVICE: Security scan reveals: (1) Critical vulnerabilities → emergency security hardening service; (2) Outdated Magento version → upgrade project; (3) PCI compliance gaps → compliance remediation; (4) No monitoring in place → ongoing security monitoring + support. Natural upsell: "We can patch these vulnerabilities in 48 hours for £X" (emergency pricing).
DELIVERY:
What you need from them: Website URL, Magento version (if known), admin email for vulnerability notifications
Timeline: 24 hours for automated scan + 48 hours for manual review = 3 days total
How delivered: PDF security report with risk score + Loom video highlighting top 3 risks + optional 15-min security briefing call
VALUE:
Perceived value: £600-£1,000 (security audits typically £500-£1,500)
Your cost to deliver: 1-2 hours (mostly automated with MageReport + expert review) = £100-£150 internal cost

OFFER #4: The "Revenue Recovery Calculator"
THE HOOK: "We'll calculate exactly how much revenue your slow Magento site is costing you every month—and show you how to get it back."
WHAT THEY GET:
Custom Revenue Loss Calculator based on their actual traffic, bounce rate, conversion rate, and average order value
Monthly revenue leakage report showing £amount lost to slow load times, cart abandonment, and checkout friction
ROI projection showing revenue recovery if speed/UX issues are fixed (with conservative estimates)
Competitive benchmark showing how much more revenue similar-sized retailers are generating with optimized sites
THE PAIN IT SOLVES: "I know our site has issues but I can't prove to my boss that fixing them will generate ROI." This translates technical problems into the language executives understand: lost money. Addresses the conversion rate optimization gap—UK data shows optimized sites can increase conversions 300-400%.
WHY IT WORKS FOR COLD TRAFFIC: Money talks. Everybody wants to know "how much is this costing me?" Framing it as "recovery" rather than "spending" shifts psychology. Using their actual GA data makes it personalized and credible. The calculator creates a tangible deliverable they can share internally to justify investment.
PSYCHOLOGICAL TRIGGER: Loss aversion + Greed. Fear of money already being lost (more powerful than potential gains). The "money left on the table" creates urgency. Appeals to the metric-driven ecommerce manager who needs ammunition for budget requests.
QUALIFICATION MECHANISM: Requires Google Analytics access (high-trust action = serious prospect). The quality of their data determines lead quality—if they have 50k+ monthly visitors and 2%+ bounce rate, they're qualified. Follow-up questions about budget authority and decision timeline reveal buying intent.
BRIDGE TO MAIN SERVICE: Calculator shows specific revenue losses: (1) £X lost to slow load times → performance optimization service; (2) £X lost to cart abandonment → checkout UX optimization; (3) £X lost to mobile issues → mobile optimization. Natural upsell: "Our optimization package costs £X but will recover £Y per month = ROI in Z months."
DELIVERY:
What you need from them: Google Analytics access (30-90 days of data), average order value, current conversion rate (if known)
Timeline: 48 hours from data access to calculator delivery
How delivered: Interactive calculator spreadsheet + PDF revenue recovery report + 20-min strategy call to walk through findings
VALUE:
Perceived value: £1,200-£1,800 (CRO analysis typically £1,000-£2,000)
Your cost to deliver: 2-3 hours (data analysis + calculation modeling) = £150-£250 internal cost

OFFER #5: The "Pre-Peak Season Health Check"
THE HOOK: "Book your free 45-minute Magento health check before Q4 peak season—we'll find the technical landmines before they explode."
WHAT THEY GET:
Live 45-minute screen-share session where your Magento expert examines their site in real-time
"Red Flag Report" documenting critical issues discovered during the session with severity rankings
Seasonal preparedness scorecard (1-10 rating) for performance, security, stability, and scalability
Prioritized action plan with "must fix before peak," "should fix soon," and "nice to have" categorizations
THE PAIN IT SOLVES: "I don't even know what I don't know about our Magento setup, and I'm terrified something will break during our busiest season." Many ecommerce managers inherited Magento sites with technical debt from previous developers. Why this matters: Q4 (Oct-Dec) represents 30-40% of annual revenue for retail; one major outage can destroy the entire year's profit.
WHY IT WORKS FOR COLD TRAFFIC: Live format builds instant trust and rapport. They get immediate feedback, not a report in 2 weeks. Interactive Q&A lets them ask burning questions. Scarcity: "Only 10 health checks available before Black Friday" creates urgency. The "health check" framing feels proactive, not desperate.
PSYCHOLOGICAL TRIGGER: Curiosity + Expert validation. The desire to have an expert "look under the hood" and confirm (or deny) their suspicions. Proactive self-image: "I'm the kind of manager who prepares early." Social proof: "Other smart managers are doing this."
QUALIFICATION MECHANISM: Live session requires real commitment (45 mins of their time + screen share). Quality of questions during session reveals sophistication. Size of issues found determines urgency. Pre-qualifying question: "What's your expected peak season traffic increase?" reveals scale. Calendar scheduling = serious intent.
BRIDGE TO MAIN SERVICE: Live session creates immediate relationship and trust. Issues discovered fall into: (1) Critical fixes needed now → emergency remediation project; (2) Hosting inadequacy → migration project; (3) Performance optimization needed → optimization retainer; (4) Everything looks good → preventative maintenance contract. Natural close: "I can fix these 3 critical items this week for £X."
DELIVERY:
What you need from them: Magento admin access, 45-minute calendar block, screen sharing capability (Zoom/Teams)
Timeline: Scheduled within 5 business days of request; report delivered within 24 hours after session
How delivered: Live Zoom session + post-session PDF report + follow-up email with recordings and action items
VALUE:
Perceived value: £500-£800 (45 mins of senior Magento expert time)
Your cost to deliver: 1.5 hours total (45-min session + 30-min report prep) = £150-£200 internal cost

PART 3: STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATION
RECOMMENDED OFFER: Black Friday Emergency Preparedness Report (Offer #1)
Why This Offer Wins:
Market Fit: Perfectly timed for October-November outreach when Black Friday panic sets in. UK retailers lost £7+ billion potential from downtime/performance issues during peak 2016 season. Addresses the #1 existential fear: "Will my site crash when it matters most?"
Differentiation: Nobody else offers 48-hour turnaround with personalized video walkthrough. Competitors charge £1,500+ for PDF reports with 1-2 week wait. The video format is memorable, shareable internally, and builds relationship vs. faceless audit.
Conversion Potential: Highest urgency due to external deadline (Black Friday). Natural qualification through timeline pressure—only serious prospects respond. Multiple upsell paths (emergency fixes, hosting migration, ongoing support). Video call creates relationship foundation for long-term client value.
Delivery Efficiency: Leverages existing Magento audit process. Can batch-deliver during Oct-Nov peak demand. Video format is faster than written reports. Templates and checklists are reusable. Senior tech can deliver 2-3 per day during high season.
Implementation Notes:
Timing is Everything: Launch campaign September 15-October 15 for maximum impact. After October 20, switch messaging to "emergency" framing with premium pricing.
Scarcity Mechanism: Limit to "first 25 UK retailers" or "10 spots remaining this month" to create urgency and prevent overwhelming delivery capacity.
Success Metric to Track: Conversion rate from video delivery to paid project. Target: 40-60% of reports should generate paid work within 30 days. Track: (1) Report requests, (2) Video delivery completion, (3) Follow-up call booking rate, (4) Project conversion, (5) Average project value, (6) Long-term retention rate.

ALTERNATIVE RECOMMENDATIONS BY SCENARIO:
If targeting year-round (not seasonal): Use Offer #2 (3-Second Site Speed Diagnostic) as it's always relevant and competitively driven.
If targeting security-conscious industries (financial, healthcare products): Lead with Offer #3 (Security Risk Scan) for maximum fear-based urgency.
If targeting CFOs/budget holders: Use Offer #4 (Revenue Recovery Calculator) as it speaks their language (ROI/revenue).
If building long-term relationships over quick wins: Deploy Offer #5 (Pre-Peak Health Check) for the live interaction and trust-building.

IMPLEMENTATION SEQUENCE (RECOMMENDED):
Q3 (July-Sept): Offer #2 (Speed Diagnostic) for awareness building
 Q4 (Oct-Nov): Offer #1 (Black Friday Preparedness) for maximum urgency
 Q1 (Jan-Mar): Offer #4 (Revenue Recovery) for New Year planning budgets
 Q2 (Apr-Jun): Offer #5 (Health Check) for relationship building before next peak

QUALIFICATION FRAMEWORK FOR ALL OFFERS:
Tier 1 Prospects (Highest Value):
Running Magento 2.4+
£1M+ annual online revenue
50k+ monthly visitors
Decision maker responds within 24 hours
Provides full access without hesitation
Multiple pain points identified
Budget authority indicated
Peak season approaching
Tier 2 Prospects (Good Value):
Running Magento 2.x (any version)
£250k-£1M annual online revenue
10k-50k monthly visitors
Decision maker responds within 48 hours
Some access provided (read-only or delayed)
1-2 pain points clearly identified
Needs to "check with team" on budget
General awareness of issues
Tier 3 Prospects (Nurture):
Running Magento 1.x or very old 2.x
<£250k annual online revenue
<10k monthly visitors
Slow response (3+ days)
Hesitant to provide access
Vague pain points
"Just looking" / information gathering
No immediate timeline

You are a senior strategy analyst whose job is to distill long-form market research and campaign planning documents into concise, high-signal research highlights.

Your task is NOT to rewrite the document.
Your task is to extract only the most important insights and compress them into a short, scannable summary that a founder, strategist, or AI system can immediately understand and use.

INPUT

You will receive a detailed document that may include:
	•	Market research
	•	Persona psychology
	•	Pain points
	•	Industry data
	•	Campaign offers
	•	Strategic recommendations
	•	Implementation notes

Assume the input is accurate and well-researched.

DOCUMENT: {{60.result}}

⸻

OUTPUT RULES (VERY IMPORTANT)
	•	Do NOT invent new insights
	•	Do NOT add fluff or commentary
	•	Do NOT repeat long explanations
	•	Do NOT use marketing buzzwords
	•	Use plain, direct language
	•	Write as if explaining to a smart operator with limited time
	•	Keep it tight and decisive

⸻

REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT (MATCH EXACTLY)

Research Highlights:

Target Persona Reality:
Summarize the lived reality of the target persona in 2–3 sentences.
Focus on:
	•	Emotional state
	•	Job pressure
	•	What they fear most
	•	What keeps them up at night

Top 3 Pain Points (in their words):
List exactly 3 short pain statements, phrased the way the market actually speaks.
No explanations here — just the pain.

Critical Market Insights:
List 4–6 hard insights or data-backed truths pulled from the research.
These should be:
	•	Numbers
	•	Patterns
	•	Competitive gaps
	•	Time-based or urgency-driven factors

Use bullets. Be concrete.

Campaign Offers Created:
List all offers concisely using this structure:
	•	#1 – Offer Name: One-line explanation of why it works
	•	#2 – Offer Name: One-line explanation
(etc.)

If one offer is clearly strongest, mark it as (RECOMMENDED) and briefly explain why in the same line.

⸻

STYLE GUIDELINES
	•	Think: internal strategy doc, not marketing copy
	•	Clarity > persuasion
	•	Short sentences > long ones
	•	Compression is the goal

If the source material is extremely long, prioritize:
	1.	Persona psychology
	2.	Pain intensity
	3.	Urgency drivers
	4.	Offer differentiation

⸻

FINAL CHECK BEFORE SUBMITTING

Before outputting, verify:
	•	Could someone understand the market in under 60 seconds?
	•	Are the insights actionable?
	•	Is this something a strategist or AI system could immediately build from?

If yes — deliver the summary.

SIX CONVERSION FRAMEWORKS
FRAMEWORK 1: Direct Offer Campaign
What it is
A straightforward campaign that clearly states the problem and the outcome. No storytelling, no long setup.
Why we run it
When the pain is obvious and the solution is easy to understand, directness outperforms creativity.
When we run it
When the prospect already understands the problem


When speed matters more than nuance


When clarity beats persuasion


How we run it for success
One clear problem


One clear outcome


One clear CTA

Want me to walk you through it?
Framework 2: Lead Magnet Campaign
What it is
A campaign that offers something tangible and valuable upfront, with no commitment. The free asset directly connects to the core service. The free asset should be good enough, someone is willing to pay for it. It also should solve a problem, that then creates a new problem that is solved by your offer.
Why we run it
Giving value first builds trust faster than claims. A good lead magnet also pre-qualifies interest because only people with the underlying problem engage.
When we run it
When trust needs to be built quickly


When the market ignores direct pitches


When the free asset naturally leads to a bigger conversation


How we run it for success
The lead magnet must be something people would normally pay for


It must solve a real sub-problem, not be generic


The CTA asks permission, not commitment


Example scripts
Straight Lead Magnet

Free Resource – Expect to Believe

But I’d never expect you to believe me without giving you something first.
I made you a {resource}. Want me to send it over?
Lead Magnet Subject Line

{FIRST_NAME} — I just finished a report on {LEADMAG}.
Would you like to see it?
FRAMEWORK 3: Loom / Video Campaign
What it is
A campaign that offers a short, personalized video breaking down a real opportunity or issue.
Why we run it
Video creates instant differentiation and credibility when it’s tied to something real. It works best when showing beats explaining.
When we run it
When personalization matters


When the opportunity is visual or tactical


When attention needs to be earned


How we run it for success
The video is positioned as the solution, not the ask


The email asks permission before sending


The video is short and specific


Example scripts
Video Permission Ask
Hey Jack,
I recently bought a fantastic jacket from your store for my sister’s birthday, and she loved it! As someone involved in e-commerce marketing, I couldn't help but notice that you haven't tapped into Amazon yet. Amazon has been a game-changer for apparel brands due to its massive traffic and buyer intent.

Want me to send it?

Mind if I share a video showing you how to fix it in 5 minutes?
FRAMEWORK 4: Education-Based Campaign (Whitepaper)
What it is
An education-first campaign framed around a whitepaper, report, or industry breakdown. Instead of pitching a service, the outreach positions the conversation as research, insight-sharing, or peer learning.
Why we run it
Education campaigns lower defenses by removing the feeling of being sold to. Prospects engage because they want to:
See how others in their space are operating


Learn what’s working before committing to change


Validate their current strategy against peers


This naturally qualifies interest and leads into a sales conversation after trust is established.
When we run it
When positioning as a thought leader matters


When selling a more complex or strategic service


When the market is skeptical of direct pitches


When the goal is higher-quality conversations over raw volume


How we run it for success
The topic must be something the market already cares about


The framing is “research” or “education,” not “marketing”


Participation feels optional and low-pressure


Insights are shared back with the prospect (early access, summary, or examples)


The transition into what we do happens after value is delivered.
Example scripts
Interview Whitepaper Outreach

We’re putting together a whitepaper on {HEADLINE}.
We’ve already spoken with {company}, {company}, and {company}.

FRAMEWORK 5: Risk Reversal Campaign
What it is
A direct offer paired with a clear guarantee or downside protection. The goal is to remove fear around trying something new.
Why we run it
Most prospects hesitate not because they don’t want results, but because they’ve been burned before. Risk reversal shifts the mental equation from “what if this fails?” to “what if this works?”
When we run it
When skepticism is high


When the outcome can be clearly defined


When confidence in delivery is strong


How we run it for success
The guarantee must be simple and believable


The outcome must be measurable


The email stays short and confident, not defensive

If we leveraged what we did for {case study} I’m confident we could {offer}.
Just did something similar where they saw {result} in {timeframe}.

We help {niche} {offer}.
Here’s the plan we’d run:
{plan}

FRAMEWORK 6: Case Study Campaign
What it is
A campaign that leads with a specific, real result achieved for another company and offers to share how it was done. The focus is not selling the service directly, but exposing a strategy that worked.
Why we run it
People are far more interested in how something worked than being pitched. A strong case study reframes the outreach as learning instead of selling, which lowers resistance and increases replies.
When we run it
When there is a clear result worth sharing


When the outcome aligns closely with what the prospect wants


When credibility and proof matter more than novelty


How we run it for success
The case study must be specific (numbers, timeframe, mechanism)


The CTA is framed as sharing the strategy, not booking a sales call


Follow-ups reinforce proof, not pressure

{AI generated first line that is very relevant to the prospect reading this email + also noting what you did for the competitor company}
